name: Franziskanerkloster Schwaz
kurzbeschreibung: Founded in 1507 by Emperor Maximilian I, the Franciscan Monastery in Schwaz houses a world-renowned Gothic cloister with 22 Passion frescoes.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Franciscan Monastery of Schwaz in the storied silver city of Schwaz in the lower Inn Valley is a cultural and artistic monument of continental renown. Situated along Gilmstraße at the foot of the Kellerjoch mountain, the late-Gothic monastic complex forms an oasis of peaceful contemplative silence within the urban core. As a sanctuary of quiet reflection and a magnificent testament to Renaissance cultural flowering in the Alps, the monastery ranks among the most remarkable cultural highlights in the Tyrolean Inn Valley. Beyond Austria's borders, the monastery is celebrated for its Gothic cloister, preserving one of Central Europe's most extensive, best-preserved monumental Passion fresco cycles.

Route & Requirements

During the early 16th century, silver mining propelled Schwaz to become the second largest city in the entire Habsburg realm. To minister to the spiritual welfare of the hardworking miners, Emperor Maximilian I founded the monastery for the Franciscan friars in 1507. By 1509 the cloister was consecrated, followed by the completion of the monastery church in 1515. The artistic crown jewel is the 200-square-meter cloister: between 1512 and 1526, the anonymous Master of the Schwaz Cloister painted a monumental Passion cycle across 22 extensive wall panels. The intricate compositions draw inspiration from woodcuts by Albrecht Dürer and Hans Schäufelein, applied in fine quill pen line work and softly layered glazing. The frescoes mirror the Renaissance epoch: biblical soldiers are depicted as contemporary Landsknecht mercenaries, and Schwaz miners appear in vivid detail. The church also impresses with Rococo stuccowork and carved choir stalls.

Visit & Arrival

The cloister and monastery church are freely accessible to visitors daily year-round from 08:00 to approximately 18:30 (in summer until 19:00). Admission is free; donations toward historic maintenance are welcomed. Guided tours can be arranged via the local tourism board. The small monastery shop offers herbal teas and remedies crafted according to monastic recipes. Transit: take Tyrol S-Bahn lines S4 or S5 to Schwaz railway station, then walk 10 minutes through the old town to Gilmstraße 1 or take the city bus directly to the Klosterkirche stop. By car: Inntal autobahn A12, exit Schwaz; park in the Stadtgalerien or Stadtplatz garages.

Tips

The entrance, church interior, and historic cloister are step-free and fully accessible for wheelchair users. Informative multi-language panels throughout the cloister explain each scene of the Passion cycle and its artistic significance. The serene, verdant inner courtyard invites visitors to rest quietly after admiring the art. Pair your visit with a walking tour of the historic Schwaz silver district and the show mine.
